svg.text: Data movement — DDR buffers and on-chip memory
Every stage is a DDR-to-DDR streaming pass. The frame never fits on-chip.
ONE ELOD PER PIPE RUN — the internal corner-turn writes SIG, so a frame OVERWRITES ITS OWN INPUT. A second run without reloading silently processes the previous run's intermediate data.
On-chip memory: 412 of 812 LSRAM blocks (50.7%), 866 uSRAM
Why so much: the corner-turn double-buffers full-width tiles so FILL and DRAIN overlap. That is exactly what took
its idle time from 41.5% to 2.0% — the memory is spent to keep the DDR port asking for data continuously.
